Subject: Performance benchmarking: multi-model fanout & tail-latency characteristics

Hi Priya,

Following up from Atlantic Cloud's RFP — we have a specific section asking for details on how Redwood handles "multi-model fanout" patterns. Our workload often fans a single API request out to 3–6 model variants (ensemble scoring + reranking) in parallel and then aggregates results. The primary concerns for our procurement and SRE teams are:

- How tail-latency behaves as concurrency increases (p50/p95/p99/p99.9).
- How cost and GPU utilization scale when multiple small models run in parallel versus a single larger model.
- Interaction with caching/KV cache (does fanout nullify caching benefits?).
- Expected warm vs cold-start differences for parallel inference.
- Test methodology: traffic shapes to simulate, sample sizes, and what evidence you can provide (raw logs, csvs) for SRE review.

Can you provide a concise test plan and sample metrics you would collect? If possible, we also want a short summary of recommended lab configuration (instance types, batch sizes, concurrency sweep) and whether you can reproduce the tests on a Redwood Dedicated reservation for a controlled run.

Thanks — happy to set up a quick call.

Simon Jackson
Platform Engineering
Atlantic Cloud

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a focused test plan (redwood_multimodel_fanout_testplan.pdf) that we use for RFPs like this; below is a compact summary and the key metrics we will collect and why.

Summary of approach (short):
- Test modes: parallel fanout (N concurrent model invocations per request) and sequential fanout (N back-to-back).
- Traffic shapes: steady-state Poisson at target QPS, bursty sawtooth to exercise autoscaling, and short spike sequences (10–30s) for tail analysis.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 concurrent requests per replica; run at 30/60/90% of measured max throughput to capture pre/post saturation behavior.
- Sample sizes: 200k tokens per sweep or 10k requests (whichever is larger) to stabilize p99.9 estimates.
- Environments: dedicated-reserved nodes (single-GPU and 4x-GPU profiles) and hosted sandbox for comparison.

Metrics collected (per-request and per-token as applicable):
- Latency percentiles: p50/p75/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 (end-to-end and model-only).
- Component breakdown: request router queuing, batching delay, model exec time, KV/prefix cache hit latency, network overhead.
- GPU metrics: utilization, memory pressure, kernel time, SM occupancy, power draw.
- Cost proxies: tokens processed, GPU-seconds, and estimated per-inference cost with current pricing.
- Error modes: timeouts, OOMs, fallback triggers, and differences when fallbacks route to a lower-capacity variant.

Key test notes and assumptions:
- For parallel fanout we run both (A) fully-parallel model servers and (B) multiplexed serial execution on a single replica to surface differences in batching dynamics.
- Caching: we include prefix-cache warmup runs and a TTL sweep to show when caching benefits amortize. Fanout can reduce effective cache reuse; we measure per-model cache hit-rate and aggregate impact.
- Warm vs cold: cold-start analysis done by cycling replicas and measuring first-request latencies across 50 cold cycles.

Deliverables we will provide after the run:
- Raw csvs with per-request timing (attached: latency_raw_results.csv), aggregated percentile tables, and a brief narrative with recommended configuration changes for your workload.
- Run notes with exact node specs, model versions, quantization flags, and kernel selection used.

Next steps: I looped Dylan (perf engineer) and Marissa (bench lead) to confirm the node profiles and to schedule a dedicated run. Are you available Wednesday 10am PT for a 30-minute lab-setup sync?

Best,

Priya Natarajan

Priya — adding a few engineering specifics that SRE/bench team will want to see in the test artifact. Quoting your summary below for context.

On Mon, Mar 8, 2027 at 12:05 PM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary of approach (short):
> - Test modes: parallel fanout (N concurrent model invocations per request) and sequential fanout (N back-to-back).

Technical clarifications and notes:
- HW config: we recommend testing on both 1xA10/A30-class and 4xA100-class nodes to show how kernel scheduling and inter-GPU copies affect parallel model execution. For Dedicated runs we can pin to a homogeneous pool.
- Batching strategy: we will test with batching disabled (per-request routing) and with continuous batching enabled. For small models in parallel, batching window (5–15ms) materially affects p95/p99.
- Kernel selection / quantization: we will run two quantization profiles (fp16 and int8 quantized) and log kernel selection. Int8 reduces exec time but can slightly increase variance under memory pressure — we'll capture this.
- Measurement artifacts: to ensure p99.9 stability we use stratified sampling across time windows and a bootstrap estimator for confidence intervals. We will annotate results where sample counts are low.
- Fanout orchestration: measure both (1) synchronous parallel invocations with aggregation at the router and (2) asynchronous pipelined invocation where partial results are returned progressively. These differ in both tail composition and perceived user latency.

I'll attach the CSV of a short lab run (latency_raw_results.csv) that demonstrates the output we provide. It includes columns: request_id, model_variant, start_ts, end_ts, model_exec_ms, batch_wait_ms, kernel_ms, gpu_util_pct, node_type.

Let me know if Atlantic Cloud wants additional traces (we can provide Zipkin/OTel spans) or raw performance counters (NVIDIA DCGM dumps) under NDA.

—Dylan
